findings.evidence: Slash.lean:54-56 — the body under `refine ... fun i _ ↦ ?_` never mentions `s` or `i` except as `g i`; `Slash.lean:62-64` is the same. `BoundedAtCusp.lean:76` supplies the sum step generically.
findings.fix: Extract `isZeroAt_rat_slash (g : GL (Fin 2) ℚ) (hf : ∀ c, IsCusp c Γ → c.IsZeroAt f k) (hc : IsCusp c Γ) : c.IsZeroAt (f ∣[k] g) k` with the current three-line body, and make the sum version `OnePoint.IsZeroAt.sum fun i _ ↦ isZeroAt_rat_slash k (g i) hf hc`.
findings.issue: The general fact proved is per-summand — `c.IsZeroAt (f ∣[k] g) k` for a single rational `g` — and the `Finset` sum is only `IsZeroAt.sum` applied on top. Stating only the sum form means a consumer with a single rational slash, or a sum that is not a bare `Finset.sum` (the `p ∤ N` term of the classical `T_p`, which is `heckeSlashUpperTri k p f` plus one further slash — see roadmap ModularForms/README.md line 409 and the UpperTriSum.lean header), must re-open-code `rw [ModularForm.rat_slash]; exact IsZeroAt.smul_iff.mp (hf _ (hc.smul_map_ratCast _))` — the very duplication this PR exists to remove.

findings.evidence: Slash.lean:62-64, identical shape to lines 54-56; Mathlib `IsBoundedAt.smul_iff` (mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/BoundedAtCusp.lean:58) is the single-element step.
findings.fix: Add `isBoundedAt_rat_slash (g : GL (Fin 2) ℚ) ... : c.IsBoundedAt (f ∣[k] g) k` and derive `isBoundedAt_sum_rat_slash` from it in one line.
findings.issue: Same under-generalization in the boundedness lemma: `isBoundedAt_sum_rat_slash` is `IsBoundedAt.sum` over a per-slash fact that is never stated.

summary: The generalization over an arbitrary Finset and rational family is correct and no hypothesis is unused, but the extracted primitive is the sum rather than the single slash: the argument itself is per-summand, and the Finset wrapper blocks the next non-sum consumer.
